steps.title: Represent four samples by one value
steps.explanation: Keep g=(-0.75,0.25,-0.25,0.75), weights (1,3,2,2) and K=8 fixed. The weighted average is 0.125, so one shared pressure-space value misses most variation.
steps.observe: Full energy is 8, represented energy 0.5 and unresolved energy 7.5. Teal, green and orange arrows show g, Pg and g−Pg on the same signed scale.

steps.title: Add one independent group value
steps.explanation: The two pairs can now have separate weighted means: 0 and 0.25. Refinement changes only the representable space, not the prescribed samples.
steps.observe: Represented energy rises to 1 and unresolved energy falls to 7; their sum stays 8. The identity defect reports zero for this authored rational fixture.

steps.title: Represent every sample
steps.explanation: With one independent value per sample, Pg equals g and every residual arrow has zero length. Refinement recovers the previously unresolved component.
steps.observe: Represented energy is 8 and unresolved energy is zero. This is an exact finite-vector representation result, not a body equilibrated with four pressures.

steps.title: Test when refinement gains nothing
steps.explanation: Now prescribe (-0.5,-0.5,0.25,0.25), already constant within each pair. Two values can represent this field completely.
steps.observe: Full and represented energies both equal 5, with zero gap. Manually select four values: no additional energy is recovered because the field was already represented.

audit.finding: The original single-field adapter showed refinement but could not demonstrate the important already-represented case.
audit.change: Add the same bounded field presets as the published standalone lab, retaining its weights, scale and energy identity.
audit.remaining: Finite weighted projection at fixed samples. No nonlinear equilibrium, pressure/displacement stability, continuous incompressibility, Hessian ordering or anatomy validation.
